Chenhuan Li

library(survival)  
library(km.ci)
library(tableone)
renal <- read.table("renal_data.txt", header = TRUE)

# data type manage
renal$medgroup <- factor(renal$medgroup, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Treatment A", "Treatment B"))
renal$sex <- factor(renal$sex, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Female", "Male"))
renal$heartfailure <- factor(renal$heartfailure, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes"))
renal$livercirrhosis <- factor(renal$livercirrhosis, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes"))
renal$eGFRstage <- factor(renal$eGFRstage) # eGFR 1-5 ，factor

## descriptive statistics
myVars <- c("age", "sex", "BMI", "heartfailure", "livercirrhosis", "eGFRstage", "status_DT")

catVars <- c("sex", "heartfailure", "livercirrhosis", "eGFRstage", "status_DT")

tab1 <- CreateTableOne(vars = myVars, 
                       strata = "medgroup", 
                       data = renal, 
                       factorVars = catVars)

print(tab1, showAllLevels = TRUE, nonnormal = c("BMI", "age"), test = FALSE)

Kaplan-Meier Curve

# 在不考虑患者其他身体条件差异的情况下，直观比较两组药物的效果。

library(survival)  
library(survminer)
## Loading required package: ggpubr
## 
## Attaching package: 'survminer'
## The following object is masked from 'package:survival':
## 
##     myeloma
km_fit <- survfit(Surv(time_DT, status_DT) ~ medgroup, data = renal)

KM_plot <- ggsurvplot(km_fit, 
           data = renal,
           pval = TRUE,            
           conf.int = TRUE,   
           risk.table = TRUE,       
           title = "Kaplan-Meier Curve: Time to Dialysis by Medication Group",
           xlab = "Time to Dialysis", 
           ylab = "Dialysis-Free Probability", 
           palette = c("#E7B800", "#2E9FDF"))  

print(KM_plot)

From Kaplan-Meier plot, we can observe a highly significant difference between the two treatment groups, with a log-rank p-value of less than 0.0001.” KM 曲线:我们可以观察到两组治疗具有极其显著的差异，Log-rank 检验的 \(p\) 值小于 0.0001

Patients in Treatment A (the yellow line) show a significantly higher dialysis-free probability compared to Treatment B (the blue line). Treatment A 组（黄色线）的无透析概率显著高于 Treatment B 组

The risk table shows that we have a sufficient sample size in both groups at the start, though the number at risk drops over time due to events and censoring. 风险表:我们在开始时两组都有充足的样本量，尽管随着事件发生和删失，风险人数随时间下降。

Cox’s Proportional Hazards Model

# holding other covariates constant
cox_model <- coxph(Surv(time_DT, status_DT) ~ medgroup + age + sex + BMI + 
                   heartfailure + livercirrhosis + eGFRstage, 
                 data = renal)

summary(cox_model)
## Call:
## coxph(formula = Surv(time_DT, status_DT) ~ medgroup + age + sex + 
##     BMI + heartfailure + livercirrhosis + eGFRstage, data = renal)

##   n= 2150, number of events= 217

## heartfailureYes      1.000144  2.718673  0.389250  2.569  0.01019 *  
## livercirrhosisYes    0.920520  2.510594  0.342956  2.684  0.00727 ** 
## eGFRstage2          -1.200585  0.301018  0.478592 -2.509  0.01212 *  
## eGFRstage3          -0.647578  0.523312  0.464083 -1.395  0.16290    
## eGFRstage4           0.548035  1.729851  0.346159  1.583  0.11338    
## eGFRstage5           2.158047  8.654221  0.319707  6.750 1.48e-11 ***

To further validate our findings and adjust for potential confounders. 验证,校正潜在的混杂因素

The results are highly robust. Even after controlling for age, BMI, comorbidities, and eGFR stages, patients on Treatment B have a 2.34 times higher hazard of the event (dialysis) compared to Treatment A, with a p-value of less than 0.0001 即使在控制了其他变量后，与治疗 A 相比，治疗 B 透析的风险增加了 2.34 倍

Variable selection

# stepwise model selection base on AIC 
optimal_model <- step(cox_model, direction = "both")

Optimal Model=Full Model AIC cares about the overall predictive performance, AIC balances the goodness-of-fit with a penalty for model complexity

Cox-Snell Residual Plot

library(survival)

# Martingale Residual 
res_mart <- residuals(optimal_model, type = "martingale")

# Cox-Snell Residual 
cs_residuals <- renal$status_DT - res_mart

fit_cs <- survfit(Surv(cs_residuals, renal$status_DT) ~ 1)

# plot X:Cox-Snell Residuals，y:Cumulative Hazard)
plot(fit_cs$time, -log(fit_cs$surv), type = "s", 
     xlab = "Cox-Snell Residuals", 
     ylab = "Cumulative Hazard", 
     main = "Cox-Snell Residual Plot for Overall Fit",
     lwd = 2)

# 45-degree reference line
abline(0, 1, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)

To confirm the overall goodness-of-fit, I derived the Cox-Snell residuals. As shown in this plot, the estimated cumulative hazard function closely follows the 45-degree reference line, especially in the main body of the data(early and middle). This indicates that the chosen model structure and baseline hazard fit the actual data well.

Hypothesis Testing

# PH Assumption - Schoenfeld Residuals
ph_optimal <- cox.zph(optimal_model)
print(ph_optimal)
##                  chisq df     p
## medgroup        0.0216  1 0.883
## age             0.0515  1 0.821
## sex             5.7893  1 0.016
## BMI             0.8033  1 0.370
## heartfailure    0.0739  1 0.786
## livercirrhosis  0.7483  1 0.387
## eGFRstage       9.7972  4 0.044
## GLOBAL         14.6410 10 0.146
# plot
Schoenfeld_plot <- ggcoxzph(ph_optimal)
print(Schoenfeld_plot)

the Hazard Ratio for each predictor remains constant over time. Mathematically, it tests the correlation between the Schoenfeld residuals and survival time.

Model diagnostics.模型诊断 GLOBAL P=0.146, the Proportional Hazards assumption holds.模型整体可靠

Schoenfeld residuals plot:the smoothed curves for our predictors remain fundamentally flat and centered around zero over time. This confirms that the Proportional Hazards assumption holds. 残差图:预测变量的平滑曲线随时间推移基本保持水平并以零为中心，这证实了比例风险假设完美成立。

sex p= 1 0.016

eGFRstage p= 4 0.044

This means that the effects of sex and eGFR stage on dialysis are not constant. plot: smoothed curve only deviates slightly from zero at the extreme tails, might be acceptable

if not acceptable, use Stratified Cox Model

#Deviance Residuals)
# 目的：检查数据里有没有“极品病人”（比如病情极其严重却活了极久，把整个模型带偏了）
# 
Deviance_plot <- ggcoxdiagnostics(optimal_model, 
                                  type = "deviance",
                                  linear.predictions = FALSE, 
                                  ggtheme = theme_bw(),
                                  title = "Deviance Residuals: Checking for Outliers")
print(Deviance_plot)
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

the data points are distributed around zero, largely bounded within the normal range, indicating an nice goodness-of-fit without severe influential outliers.

Stratified Cox Model

# 假设对 sex 和 eGFRstage 进行分层
stratified_model <- coxph(Surv(time_DT, status_DT) ~ medgroup + age + BMI + 
                          heartfailure + livercirrhosis + 
                          strata(sex) + strata(eGFRstage), data = renal)
summary(stratified_model)
## Call:
## coxph(formula = Surv(time_DT, status_DT) ~ medgroup + age + BMI + 
##     heartfailure + livercirrhosis + strata(sex) + strata(eGFRstage),

The HR for medgroup Treatment B is now 2.37 (previously 2.34), shifted slightly, and the P-value remains significant at 4.47e-09. This conclusion still reliable after removing the influence of pH violation.

Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) model

library(survival)
#  WeibullAFT
aft_model <- survreg(Surv(time_DT, status_DT) ~ medgroup + age + BMI + heartfailure + livercirrhosis + sex + eGFRstage, data = renal, dist = "weibull")
summary(aft_model)
## 
## Call:
## survreg(formula = Surv(time_DT, status_DT) ~ medgroup + age + 
##     BMI + heartfailure + livercirrhosis + sex + eGFRstage, data = renal, 
##     dist = "weibull")
##                        Value Std. Error     z       p
## (Intercept)          2.05034    0.29405  6.97 3.1e-12
## medgroupTreatment B -0.55466    0.08799 -6.30 2.9e-10
## age                  0.00833    0.00278  2.99  0.0028
## BMI                  0.00994    0.00639  1.56  0.1195
## heartfailureYes     -0.63924    0.24130 -2.65  0.0081
## livercirrhosisYes   -0.59176    0.21423 -2.76  0.0057
## sexMale              0.19287    0.09143  2.11  0.0349
## eGFRstage2           0.75795    0.29967  2.53  0.0114
## eGFRstage3           0.41066    0.28914  1.42  0.1555
## eGFRstage4          -0.32736    0.21679 -1.51  0.1310
## eGFRstage5          -1.34751    0.21234 -6.35 2.2e-10
## Log(scale)          -0.47464    0.05300 -8.96 < 2e-16
## 
## Scale= 0.622 
## 
## Weibull distribution
## Loglik(model)= -644.1   Loglik(intercept only)= -847.4
##  Chisq= 406.55 on 10 degrees of freedom, p= 3.8e-81 
## Number of Newton-Raphson Iterations: 12 
## n= 2150

Treatment B has a highly significant negative coefficient (-0.55), meaning it significantly accelerates the time to dialysis. Being on Treatment B ‘accelerates’ the disease progression, shrinking the dialysis-free time by about \(1-\exp(-0.55466) \approx 0.43\) = 43% compared to Treatment A.

beta_aft <- coef(aft_model)
scale_val <- aft_model$scale

# dividing the negative AFT coefficients by the scale parameter(log Hazard Ratios)
beta_ph <- -beta_aft / scale_val

# convert the results to Hazard Ratios (HR)
HR_converted <- exp(beta_ph)

aft_to_hr_table <- data.frame(
  AFT_Coefficient = beta_aft,
  Converted_Cox_Coef = beta_ph,
  Converted_HR = HR_converted
)
print(round(aft_to_hr_table[-1, ], 3))
##                     AFT_Coefficient Converted_Cox_Coef Converted_HR
## medgroupTreatment B          -0.555              0.892        2.439
## age                           0.008             -0.013        0.987
## BMI                           0.010             -0.016        0.984
## heartfailureYes              -0.639              1.028        2.794
## livercirrhosisYes            -0.592              0.951        2.589
## sexMale                       0.193             -0.310        0.733
## eGFRstage2                    0.758             -1.218        0.296
## eGFRstage3                    0.411             -0.660        0.517
## eGFRstage4                   -0.327              0.526        1.693
## eGFRstage5                   -1.348              2.166        8.724

The converted HR for Treatment B is 2.439, which confirms Cox findings (HR=2.34，2.37),
